title: Batangas City holds 'bokashi ball' throwing for river restoration
content_lead:
LUCENA CITY - The Batangas City government led a "bokashi ball" throwing event at Calumpang Bridge as part of its efforts to rehabilitate the river and improve its water quality.

Held as part of the city's 57th Foundation Day celebration, hurling "bokashi balls" aims to restore river quality, strengthen environmental protection measures, and encourage greater community participation in keeping local waterways clean, the City Public Information Office (PIO) said in a report on Tuesday.

"Bokashi balls", also known as mud balls, originated in Japan, where they are widely used to revive polluted waterways.

READ: Bayanihan and corporate social impact

They contain beneficial microorganisms that help break down organic waste, reduce foul odors, and decompose sludge accumulated in contaminated bodies of water, the PIO said, citing City Environment Officer Oliver Gonzales. Bokashi balls can also help improve soil quality.

According to the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), a single bokashi ball can help treat approximately one cubic meter of sludge-laden water. This form of biotechnology has been used across the country, such as in the Manila Bay watershed.

"Through programs such as this, the Batangas City government continues to promote a clean, safe, and greener environment for the benefit of both present and future generations," the PIO said.

The Calumpang River has a catchment area of about 472 square kilometers. It forms the southeastern boundary of Batangas City's urban center before emptying into Batangas Bay.

Local authorities said the river has faced increasing environmental pressure from rapid urbanization and agricultural runoff over the years, prompting the implementation of watershed protection measures and river cleanup initiatives./coa

title: Helping communities grow together
content_lead:
FIFTY-NINE residents of Barangay Sorosoro Ibaba in Batangas pooled together P11,800 in 1969 to put up a small community store. Today, that organization has grown into the Sorosoro Ibaba Development Cooperative (SIDC), one of the country's largest agri-based cooperatives with more than 81,000 members, operations spanning agriculture, financial services, retail and wholesale, and assets of about P7.7 billion.

SIDC is not an isolated success story. The Ayala Coop which traces its roots to 1995, when 21 employees of the Ayala Group organized the cooperative with an initial capital of P10,500. Since then, it has expanded into one of the country's largest employee-owned cooperatives, with nearly 40,000 members nationwide, capitalization exceeding P5 billion and total assets of more than P6 billion.

For the past 36 years, the CDA has been the government's lead agency for the cooperative sector. Created through Republic Act 6939 in 1990, it was tasked with promoting the growth of cooperatives while ensuring they remain faithful to the principles on which they were founded. While registration and regulation remain at the heart of its mandate, the agency also provides technical assistance, promotes good governance and works with local governments and national agencies to help cooperatives expand.

Since assuming the chairmanship in 2025, Undersecretary Alexander B. Raquepo has placed much of the agency's attention on expanding support for micro and small cooperatives, improving coordination with local governments and national agencies, and carrying out the Philippine Cooperative Development Plan 2025-2028. Those priorities have shaped many of the programs introduced this year.

Working alongside the CDA Board, Administrator Emmanuel Santiaguel oversees the day-to-day implementation of the agency's programs, from cooperative registration and regulation to education, technical assistance and field operations carried out through its regional offices.

title: ¿Por qué se llama Comarca Lagunera? Estos son los 15 municipios que la conforman
content_lead:
El origen del nombre de la Comarca Lagunera y los municipios que la conforman. (Especial)

Hablar de la Comarca Lagunera es mucho más que decir que es una región ubicada entre algunos municipios de Coahuila y Durango. Para miles de personas esta región representa su hogar, años de historia y una identidad compartida.

Aunque hoy es conocida por su desarrollo industrial, agrícola y económico; el origen de su nombre se remonta a una época antigua, en la que el agua fue el principal factor que dio vida a una de las zonas más importantes del norte de México.

¿Por qué la Comarca Lagunera tiene este nombre?

La Laguna, como también se le conoce a la Comarca Lagunera, recibe este nombre debido a la gran cantidad de lagunas que existieron en el territorio. De acuerdo con el Servicio Geológico Mexicano llegaron a contabilizarse hasta 13 cuerpos de agua, entre ellos la emblemática Laguna de Mayrán que era alimentada por los ríos Nazas y Aguanaval.

El Río Nazas, conocido por muchos como el "Padre Nazas" tuvo una gran influencia en el nacimiento y crecimiento de la región, pues a diferencia de la mayoría de los ríos mexicanos, este no desembocaba en el mar, sino que terminaba su recorrido en la Laguna de Mayrán, formando así una cuenca que transformó el entorno semidesértico en tierras fértiles, favoreciendo la agricultura, la ganadería y el establecimiento de poblaciones que hoy forman parte de la Comarca Lagunera.

¿Dónde se encuentra la Comarca Lagunera y qué municipios la conforman?

La Comarca Lagunera se localiza entre el suroeste de Coahuila y el noreste de Durango. La región destaca por su actividad industrial, minera, comercial y de servicios, así como por su conectividad, pues cuenta con importantes carreteras federales, el ferrocarril Durango-Torreón-Monclova y el Aeropuerto Internacional Francisco Sarabia, en Torreón.

La Comarca se integra por 15 municipios, distribuidos entre Durango y Coahuila.

title: El Sistema Cutzamala tiene agua garantizada hasta 2027: así logró recuperarse de la crisis de 2024
content_lead:
El Valle de México, la región más poblada del país, tiene unos meses de "alivio" en cuanto a la dotación de agua potable se refiere gracias a que el Sistema Cutzamala ha logrado mantener un suministro de 15.3 metros cúbicos por segundo (m³/s), o lo que es lo mismo, 15,300 litros por segundo, lo que representa una de las dotaciones más grandes en sus cuatro décadas de operación.

Tras haber tocado niveles críticos de apenas 6 m³/s en junio de 2024, la actual gestión reporta un almacenamiento del 71% (561 millones de m³), lo que garantiza el abasto proyectado por parte del área técnica de la Comisión Nacional del Agua (Conagua), y bajo las condiciones actuales, hasta diciembre de 2027.

Sin embargo, las lluvias no son el único factor que ayuda a que el abasto de agua potable en el Valle de México se mantenga estable, sino también a la operación que ha hecho Conagua en el Sistema Cutzamala, afirmó la directora general del Organismo de Cuenca Aguas del Valle de México (OCAVM), Citlalli Peraza Camacho.

"La presa Valle de Bravo fue una de las que más afectó esta sequía hace aproximadamente dos años; sin embargo, la Conagua realizó una operación donde lejos de hacer una extracción, que esa es la vocación de la presa, hizo una inyección. La recuperación de la presa Valle de Bravo fue uno de los mejores aciertos en cuestión de operación hídrica del Sistema Cutzamala", aseguró en entrevista.

La funcionaria explicó que se ha transitado de un gasto fijo a una "operación variable". Este modelo permite ajustar la entrega de agua de manera proporcional al almacenamiento real, evitando el agotamiento acelerado de las presas.

Para lograr esta precisión, el sistema abandonó las mediciones manuales con regletas para implementar sensores automáticos con monitoreo las 24 horas en presas clave como Valle de Bravo, Villa Victoria y El Bosque, y que no solo mide el almacenamiento, sino otros factores como las lluvias, viento y temperatura.

title: La CHS ultima una nueva versión de las obras contra avenidas en El Albujón tras el freno del Ministerio | La Verdad
content_lead:
La Confederación Hidrográfica del Segura ultima el proyecto que restaurará un tramo de la rambla de El Albujón, en su parte alta, para que sirva ... de zona de laminación de avenidas en episodios de lluvias intensas. El organismo público que dirige Mario Urrea parece haber encontrado una solución al freno impuesto por el Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica a la anterior versión de las obras, que tenían un enfoque más artificial y con mayor dependencia del hormigón.

El proyecto saldría a licitación con un presupuesto de casi tres millones de euros a finales de 2026 tras dos años de retraso por ese parón administrativo; las obras se ejecutarían en 2027. La CHS ha optado por seguir el espíritu del Marco de Actuaciones Prioritarias para recuperar el Mar Menor (MAPMM) y ha priorizado en el diseño las soluciones basadas en la naturaleza, un enfoque centrado en la restauración de los ecosistemas y sus entornos por el que aboga el Miteco.

Los trabajos, cuyos primeros detalles ya avanzó LA VERDAD hace un año, se centrarán en remodelar la amplia curva del cauce de El Albujón a su paso por la pedanía de El Estrecho de Fuente Álamo. La CHS calculó que será necesario expropiar una veintena de parcelas y llevar a cabo movimientos de tierra en tres áreas de este tramo para mejorar la retención de riadas y evitar desbordamientos aguas abajo. El proyecto prevé disminuir el contenido de sólidos y contaminantes del agua que llega al Mar Menor a través de la rambla.

La recuperación hidrológica de la cabecera de El Albujón se completará con otras líneas de actuación previstas, como la partida de ayudas económicas para actuar en fincas privadas ubicadas a una altitud de entre 150 y 250 metros sobre el nivel de la laguna. title: El Gobierno inyecta dos millones a un proyecto liderado por la UMH de Elche para reducir la contaminación del Mar Menor
content_lead:
Un modelo para que el manejo extensivo del ganado no sea incompatible con la recuperación de los suelos, el aumento de la biodiversidad y la disminución de los efectos contaminantes sobre el Mar Menor. Es el reto que persigue la Universidad Miguel Hernández (UMH) de Elche, que liderará uno de los proyectos de investigación más ambiciosos para la recuperación ambiental tras obtener una inyección de casi dos millones de euros del Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (Miteco).

La iniciativa, denominada Zoosimbiosis. Ganadería extensiva regenerativa. Es decir, el reto es que el terreno quede en mejores condiciones que antes por lo que en lugar de limitarse a producir carne o leche, el ganado también ayuda a fertilizar, controlar la vegetación, aumentar la biodiversidad y reducir restos nocivos que acaban en el mar.

title: En La Laguna, ciudadanos buscan recuperar el río Nazas y el acuífero

Ciudadanos y especialistas buscan recuperar el río urbano y frenar la sobreexplotación del acuífero para devolverle vida al Nazas y garantizar el futuro de La Laguna.

M+.- En el río Nazas pasa de todo, menos agua. Por su enorme cauce de tierra seca pueden encontrarse tiraderos clandestinos de basura, escombros y residuos; en algunos sectores se utiliza como vialidad improvisada y también ha sido escenario de eventos deportivos y actividades recreativas.

Para muchos jóvenes de la Comarca Lagunera, consultados por MILENIO, el río que divide a Torreón, Coahuila, y Lerdo, Durango, nunca ha sido un río permanente, sino precisamente eso: un enorme espacio vacío atravesando la zona metropolitana.

La imagen del Nazas convertido en un corredor de tierra seca ha acompañado durante generaciones a los habitantes de La Laguna.

Sin embargo, el Nazas no es un río cualquiera para el norte de México. Su cuenca atraviesa buena parte de la historia de La Laguna y durante siglos fue el hilo de agua que conectó comunidades, tierras de cultivo y ciudades que hoy concentran millones de habitantes.

Te recomendamos...

Desde la Sierra Madre Occidental, en Durango, el Nazas recorre cientos de kilómetros antes de internarse en la Comarca y alimentar el sistema de presas que transformó el paisaje del desierto; en su recorrido dio origen a lagunas, sostuvo la agricultura y terminó por convertirse en el corazón de una región que aprendió a vivir alrededor de su cauce.

Hoy, sin embargo, ese río que alguna vez marcó el ritmo de la vida lagunera llega a la zona metropolitana convertido, durante buena parte del año, en un enorme lecho seco.

title: El laboratorio a cielo abierto del Mar Menor | La Verdad

La cuenca vertiente del Mar Menor alberga ahora un mosaico de experiencias reales e innovadoras destinadas a lograr una transformación agrícola capaz de convivir con ... la laguna en un territorio que lleva décadas resonando en el mundo por sus crisis ambientales. A partir de ahora es más que posible que sea también conocido por sus soluciones disruptivas, como la captura de insectos con IA en los cultivos, y la fertilización de suelos con microalgas o minerales. Igual que en el pasado los agricultores del Campo de Cartagena despuntaron con el pimiento, el melón, el brócoli y la alcachofa, los últimos ensayos apuntan a introducir nuevos cultivos, como la pitaya, la quinoa y el amaranto. title: Reutilizan sedimentos de la Laguna Primera de Palos para proteger suelos y humedal
content_lead:
Fundación Moeve, la Junta de Andalucía, el Ayuntamiento de Palos de la Frontera y los agricultores locales han puesto en marcha un proyecto para construir una trampa de sedimentos que permite reutilizar los materiales acumulados en la Laguna Primera de Palos y así recuperar suelos agrícolas perdidos por erosión.

Gracias a esta iniciativa, la biodiversidad en la zona y la agricultura trabajan en conjunto, apoyándose en un modelo de economía circular, según explica Fundación Moeve.

La trampa de sedimentos está diseñada para combatir uno de los principales problemas del humedal: la acumulación de arenas erosionadas que llegan a la laguna arrastradas por la escorrentía, lo que acelera el depósito de sedimentos.

Funcionamiento y diseño de la trampa de sedimentos

La construcción de esta infraestructura, promovida por Fundación Moeve junto con la Consejería de Sostenibilidad y Medio Ambiente, el Ayuntamiento y el sector agrícola, implicó la retirada de cerca de 10.000 metros cúbicos de arena para crear un espacio de charca previo a la laguna principal.

Este espacio favorece la decantación de la materia sólida en suspensión antes de que el agua entre a la laguna. Además, su diseño incorpora pequeñas islas y áreas someras que ralentizan el flujo, permiten el crecimiento de vegetación y crean nuevos microhábitats para aves acuáticas y otras especies.

La trampa no solo retiene sedimentos, sino que también fija nutrientes: parte se queda con los sedimentos depositados y otra parte es absorbida por la vegetación, lo que reduce la llegada excesiva de nutrientes al vaso principal y mejora la calidad del agua disminuyendo su turbidez.

De acuerdo con Fundación Moeve, esta solución "basada en la naturaleza" aprovecha procesos naturales para minimizar la colmatación y mejorar el ecosistema, al tiempo que ofrece hábitats de interés para la biodiversidad. title: 9 de cada 10 murcianos pagarían más por naranjas producidas con agricultura regenerativa
content_lead:
¿Pagaría un 30% más por un kilo de naranjas si estas fueran producidas mediante agricultura regenerativa? El 90% de los murcianos así lo haría, según una investigación de la Universidad de Murcia (UMU) publicada en la revista científica Agronomy Journal, que señala que los ciudadanos estarían dispuestos a pagar un sobreprecio de 0,45 euros el kilo, hasta llegar a los 1,95 euros (el estudio sitúa un precio medio de 1,50 euros por kilo).

El análisis socioeconómico revela que tanto la edad como los ingresos del hogar ejercen una influencia positiva sobre la disposición total a pagar. En concreto, los efectos indican un aumento de 0,01 euros por kilo por cada año adicional de edad y de 0,10 euros por cada 1.000 euros adicionales de ingresos anuales.

La investigación, que busca analizar la percepción que los murcianos tienen sobre la agricultura regenerativa, ha sido desarrollada por el Grupo de Economía Agraria y Desarrollo Rural de UMU, que dirige el catedrático José Miguel Martínez-Paz. El trabajo se enmarca en su línea de colaboración con la Asociación Interprofesional de Limón y Pomelo (Ailimpo), y forma parte de la tesis doctoral en curso de Gonzalo Martínez García, con la participación del doctor Rafael Olmos Ruiz.

title: Los restos de la selva del espinal
content_lead:
La reserva natural educativa "Montecito de Lovera" está en Cerrito, a unos 60 kilómetros de Paraná, junto a la ruta nacional 12 y a la provincial 8, donde funciona desde fines de 2001.

Originalmente, esta área estaba ocupada por bosques nativos de la región fitogeográfica del Espinal, y fue modificándose con las actividades de los colonizadores que desde fines del siglo XIX, se dedicaron fundamentalmente a la agricultura.

El avance de los sembrados, últimamente el devastador de la soja, ha producido profundos cambios y una disminución notable de la superficie ocupada por el bosque nativo, creando un paisaje en mosaico de parcelas cultivadas y relictos de montes.

A principios de siglo los bosques del Espinal cubrían casi un 40 por ciento de nuestro territorio continental, hoy esa superficie no llega al 12 por ciento y solo el 0,1 por ciento está representado en nuestro sistema Nacional de Áreas Protegidas.

El "Montecito de Lovera" está en el extremo noreste de la localidad de Cerrito y coincide con el comienzo de una cuenca que comprende un sistema de arroyos que desaguan en el río Paraná, distante 17 kilómetros, y conecta con un número importante de corredores de bosques en galería. Este sistema permite mantener una rica diversidad en el predio destinado a la reserva.

El área protegida tiene una extensión de 6 hectáreas, las especies arbóreas dominantes son el algarrobo, ñandubay, espinillo, chañar, talita, palmera caranday; y en dicho predio se encuentran representados distintos tipos de ambientes, desde el bosque maduro cerrado, bosque bajo abierto, pastizal, zonas bajas anegadas y laguna.

Desde hace varias generaciones el "Montecito de Lovera" tuvo un uso recreativo. Los abuelos hacían allí los pic-nics de la primavera y no son pocos los que han pescado en la laguna o practicaron tiros de gomera contra la tuna.

title: Qué traen los camalotes que llegan a las costas de Santa Fe en plena crecida del Paraná

Camalotes en las costas de Santa Fe y Rosario

Este tipo de plantas acuáticas invasivas cumple un rol ecológico clave en la recuperación de los humedales, tan castigados por los incendios y las sequías históricas. No se trata sólo de la especie Pontederia crassipes, sino del "camalotal" propio de la vegetación y sedimentos esenciales para el ecosistema que el caudal arrastra a su paso desde la parte superior de la Cuenca del Plata y desciende río abajo.

La docente de la cátedra de Ecología de la Facultad de Ciencias Agrarias de la Universidad Nacional de Rosario (UNR), Graciela Klekailo, admitió que es una vegetación pintoresca, digna de apreciar y que favorece al ecosistema del humedal, pero también obliga a ser precavidos.

"Este camalotal se puede ver cuando crece el río. Es muy lindo de apreciar cuando esta vegetación aparece flotando por el río, pero también puede transformarse en un problema. Llega como consecuencia de precipitaciones abundantes río arriba a raíz del fenómeno de El Niño o cuando se abren las compuertas de las represas de Paraguay y Brasil, justamente por el gran caudal de agua", explicó Klekailo en declaraciones a La Capital.

La especialista aseguró que la presencia de este camalotal es parte de la dinámica propia del río. "No tenemos que olvidarnos que el agua es la que dicta la dinámica del humedal como sistema. Es el fuego el que no debería estar presente ahí en el humedal y el agua y esta vegetación viene un poco a devolverle la vida al río", argumentó.

title: Giant clams survive, thrive in Batangas marine sanctuaries
content_lead:
LUCENA CITY -- Giant clams (Tridacna gigas) seeded in the municipal waters off Lian and Nasugbu in Batangas province more than a decade ago continue to survive and thrive in protected marine areas.

In a report on Friday, Aug. 7, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR)-Calabarzon said giant clams planted in 2015 and 2016 in locally managed marine sanctuaries and protected areas in the two municipalities remain healthy.

The giant clams were seeded through the efforts of the DENR's Community Environment and Natural Resources Office (CENRO) in Calaca in partnership with local communities and other stakeholders.

READ: Cadiz City goes after giant clams' killers

"Based on the latest monitoring, the giant clams have reached an average length of 2.25 feet," the DENR said.

The agency said the giant clams remain safe within the marine sanctuaries through the continuing protection and monitoring efforts of CENRO-Calaca and its local partners.

Locally known as "taklobo," the giant clam is the world's largest bivalve mollusk. It is classified as critically endangered on the Red List of the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN).

Giant clams are also protected under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), an international agreement among governments designed to ensure that trade in wild animals and plants does not threaten their survival.

The harvesting, selling, purchasing, and transporting of giant clams is prohibited under Republic Act No. 10654, or the Philippine Fisheries Code.

Beyond their value as food, giant clams are also targeted for their massive shells, which have been used as materials for jewelry, chandeliers, religious icons and other products.

Their valuable shells have made the endangered species a target of illegal trade, with some smugglers reportedly turning to giant clams as substitutes for ivory.

title: Nasugbu, Batangas declares state of calamity due to Maymay
content_lead:
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.

The Municipality of Nasugbu in Batangas has declared a state of calamity in the aftermath of Tropical Storm Maymay.

The resolution issued by the Office of Sangguniang Bayan cited homes and establishments were submerged in water for days, "which resulted to slow movements of life and economic activities."

The council also noted emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases, such as Dengue and Japanese Encephalitis, within the municipality.

The resolution also cited flooding in low-lying areas and areas in riverbanks.

"Resolved further, that the Municipal Mayor, Hon. Antonio A. Barcelon, be authorized to utilize the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) Quick Reaction Fund (QRF) C.Y. 2026 for emergency relief, rescue, and rehabilitation activities," it read.

Maymay left the Philippine landmass on August 6.

Data from the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council showed that 5.1 million individuals were affected by the combined effects of the Habagat, Maymay, and Tropical Depression Luis. -- VAL, GMA News

title: Lian, Batangas residents evacuated due to 'habagat'
content_lead:

Balibago, due to the effects of a low-pressure area (LPA) and the intensified southwest monsoon, or "habagat", on Tuesday, August 18.

CGSS Lian coordinated with the officials of Barangay Balibago and safely transported the evacuated residents to the Balibago Elementary School, the designated evacuation center. The evacuees were safely evacuated and are currently staying at the evacuation center.

CGSS Lian continues to monitor the situation and coordinate with relevant agencies and the local government unit (LGU).

The PCG also reminded residents in flood-prone areas to evacuate immediately and heed local government advisories should weather conditions worsen.

While the Coast Guard Sub-Station (CGSS) Lemery, in coordination with the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (MDRRMO) San Luis, Batangas, conducted a clearing and debris removal operation at Brgy. Poblacion, Purok 6, San Luis, on Aug. 18 following the effects of the enhanced Southwest Monsoon.

Upon arrival, the team found a fallen tree and accumulated debris obstructing the waterway and drainage canal, causing muddy rainwater to accumulate and posing a potential flooding risk to nearby residential areas. The team removed the fallen branches and debris to restore the flow of water and mitigate the risk of flooding.

CGSS Lemery continues to coordinate with concerned agencies and barangay officials and monitor the area for further incidents within its area of responsibility. (AOR)

title: Coming Full Circle: From 4Ps Beneficiary To CPA, Public Servant | Journal Online
content_lead:
Aina Lou Atienza is a Certified Public Accountant (CPA) and Municipal Accountant in her hometown of San Nicolas, Batangas.

When Aina Lou sits at the planning table for the Municipal Advisory Council of San Nicolas, she does not just look at administrative files or budget allocations.

Instead, Aina sees the faces of her own family reflected in the records of the indigent citizens they aim to uplift.

Long before Aina became a department head who helped steer the town's social programs, she was at the receiving end of the programs.

"Dati benepisyaryo po ako ng isang government program, ngayon part na ako ng government," Aina shared with the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), her voice carrying the quiet pride of someone who has weathered the storm and returned to guide others to shore.

Past forged by struggles

Aina's journey into public service was forged in the quiet struggles of a farming family.

While growing up, a vast majority of their livelihood depended on her father's sweet potato crops. Because the root crop required immense patience before yielding a harvest, financial uncertainty was a constant challenge in their home.

"Yung tanim ng father ko ay kamote. So, 9 months to 1 year bago po mag harvest. So, talagang merong times na 'yung tindahan lang 'yung source of income ng buong pamilya," Aina recalled.

Despite the hard reality of making both ends meet, Aina's parents built a fortress of love and hard work around their children.

The parents absorbed the brunt of the hardship, ensuring that Aina and her three siblings never had to overthink whether there would be food on the table or money for school the next day.

title: Analog missions, open drone data focus of PH Space Week 2026
content_lead:
THE Philippine Space Agency is calling on the nation to observe Philippine Space Week from Aug. 8 to 14, 2026, advancing a national space mandate recently bolstered by explicit support from President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. during his State of the Nation Address.

Highlighting plans for a 2027 liquid-fueled sounding rocket test launch in Cagayan, Marcos declared that the province is geographically and economically primed to serve as the country's gateway to space and host its first spaceport. He affirmed that the nation will launch a rocket into space, marking a major transition toward domestic launch capabilities and regional space integration.

Organized under the theme "Navigating Tomorrow," the annual weeklong observance commemorates the passage of Republic Act 11363, also known as the Philippine Space Act, enacted on Aug. 8, 2019. Established by Proclamation No. 302, series of 2023, Philippine Space Week highlights the contributions of Filipino scientists and demonstrates how space data supports disaster risk reduction, environmental monitoring, agriculture, and national security.

The agency will host a public exhibit on Aug. 9 at Quantum Skyview in Gateway Mall 2, Araneta City, Quezon City. Running from 10 a.m. to 9 p.m., the interactive showcase will feature Philippine space assets, scientific demonstrations, and educational programs detailing practical applications of orbital telemetry.

A central highlight of the day is the formal introduction of the eight-member crew participating in the Analog Habitat Waypoint Mission in Batangas this September. Organizers will detail how these researchers will undergo a 24-hour simulated spaceflight inside a specialized terrestrial habitat, testing physiological, operational, and life-support constraints to support broader human spaceflight research.

title: Bacoor City suspends classes as monsoon rains persist
content_lead:
LUCENA CITY - The local government of Bacoor City in Cavite suspended classes at all levels in public and private schools on Tuesday (August 11), due to the continuing inclement weather.

The city government urged residents to prioritize their safety, stay indoors as much as possible, and to continue monitoring official weather and government advisories.

READ: Walang pasok: Class, work suspensions on Aug. 11

The suspension is consistent with the provisions of Department of Education (DepEd) Order No. 37, series of 2022, which provides for the automatic suspension of classes at all levels, whether face-to-face or online, when the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) issues a tropical cyclone wind signal, an orange or red rainfall warning, or a flood warning.

Classes are likewise suspended when any of these warnings or signals are issued while classes are already ongoing.

Local chief executives may also suspend classes in their respective jurisdictions whenever weather conditions pose a risk to students and school personnel, even in the absence of an automatic suspension.

Pagasa forecast that heavy rains associated with the enhanced southwest monsoon, or "habagat", would continue until Wednesday (August 12) although rainfall is expected to gradually weaken beginning Tuesday.

The weather bureau urged the public, particularly residents in affected areas, to remain vigilant and rely on official advisories issued by government agencies.

Meanwhile, another weather disturbance, Tropical Storm Peilou, was being monitored outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility. /jpv

Low-lying cities and municipalities in Cavite have long been vulnerable to flooding as runoff from upland areas flows toward lower communities during periods of heavy rain.

Residents have endured recurring floods for years, with some areas experiencing rapid increases in water levels after prolonged heavy rainfall.

The persistent problem has raised questions over existing flood-control measures and calls for longer-term solutions as development continues across the province.

Cavite has seen rapid expansion of commercial establishments, infrastructure, expressways and road networks in recent years, improving connectivity and generating economic activity.

title: Cavite Floods Worsen as Habagat Rains Persist; Kawit, Imus and Other Towns Reel From Chest-Deep Waters
content_lead:
Cavite has received persistent rainfall over the past several days, with parts of the province placed under a red rainfall warning amid the continued downpour.

In Kawit, floodwaters rose to chest- and head-high levels in some areas, forcing residents to again contend with a perennial problem, particularly during prolonged periods of heavy rain.

Located in the lower portion of the province, Kawit serves as a catch basin for water flowing from Cavite's upland areas, leaving several communities vulnerable to flooding when waterways overflow.

Other areas, including Noveleta, Imus, Bacoor, Rosario and Cavite City, also continued to experience flooding as the Habagat battered northern Cavite.

The recurring floods have renewed concerns over the adequacy of existing drainage and flood-control systems in preventing sudden rises in water levels in communities long identified as flood-prone.

Some residents have also raised concerns over the ongoing construction connecting the Cavite-Laguna Expressway (CALAX) to CAVITEX, claiming portions of the project may have affected existing waterways that previously served as natural channels for floodwaters from nearby barangays.

CALAX management, however, said the flooding should not be attributed solely to the expressway project, stressing that several factors could be involved, including the volume of rainfall and existing drainage conditions.

"The Cavite-Laguna Expressway (CALAX) management understands the concerns of communities affected by the recent flooding in nearby areas of Kawit and Imus, particularly following the heavy rainfall experienced in the area," the management said.

title: Joy Barcoma urges Filipinos to choose wisely in 2028 elections amid flooding
content_lead:
MANILA, Philippines -- Beauty queen and TV host Joy Barcoma urged Filipinos to make wiser choices in the 2028 national elections, citing the plight of communities forced to evacuate because of flooding.

Joy made the call after personally witnessing the conditions of residents affected by flooding in Kawit, Cavite, during a recent episode of GMA 7's morning program "Unang Hirit."

The program conducted a relief operation for evacuees in coordination with the Kapuso Foundation and visited residents who had been temporarily staying at an evacuation center.

In a Facebook post, Joy shared a video showing the conditions inside the evacuation center, which had also been affected by floodwaters.

"Hello po, mga tao. Nandito po tayo ngayon sa baha at kung hindi n'yo po naitatanong, maulan po dito ngayon," Joy said.

"At nandito po tayo sa evacuation center na supposedly po ay dapat ligtas na lugar po para sa ating mga kababayan. Pero kung makikita n'yo, kahit evacuation center ho natin ay binabaha," she added.

The situation prompted Joy to remind voters about the importance of choosing public officials in the 2028 elections.

She said electing the right leaders could help address long-standing problems involving flooding and disaster preparedness.

"So, sana ho ayusin na ho natin ang mga desisyon natin sa 2028, para hindi na po nakakaranas ng ganitong klaseng inconvenience 'yung mga kababayan ho natin na nakakaranas po ng pagbaha at siyempre nangangailangang lumikas sa panahon po ng habagat o ng bagyo at tuloy-tuloy na pag-ulan," she said.

Joy's remarks come as several communities continue to face the effects of heavy rains and flooding during the rainy season, highlighting the challenges faced by Filipinos who are forced to leave their homes during severe weather.

title: Need for emergency feeding of children, part 2
content_lead:
The Philippine government has several programs to combat child undernutrition. The two largest are the Supplementary Feeding Program (SFP) of the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) and the School-Based Feeding Program (SBFP) of the Department of Education (DepEd). The SFP targets children three to five years old enrolled in Child Development Centers (daycare centers) and Supervised Neighborhood Play groups.

The program provides daily nutritious hot meals (and, in some areas, milk) for 180 feeding days in 2026. It includes nutrition education for parents and caregivers, along with regular monitoring of the children’s weight and nutritional status. Local government units (LGUs) get involved under the Masustansyang Pagkain para sa Batang Pilipino Act. This year, the DSWD expanded the program to serve more than 1.8 million children nationwide, backed by a larger budget and a longer feeding period.

DepEd’s School-Based Feeding Program focuses on public school learners, especially those identified as wasted, severely wasted, or otherwise nutritionally at-risk. The program provides daily nutritious meals during the school year, milk feeding in many schools, and regular health and nutrition assessments. On July 8, 2026, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. announced the nationwide expansion of the school feeding program, stating that the government intends to broaden coverage so that more learners receive nutritious meals while also supporting the Filipino farmers who supply the food. True enough, this program was given prominence in his State of the Nation Address (SONA) yesterday.

The government also supports child nutrition through the National Nutrition Council and the Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition. Maternal and child nutrition services of the Department of Health include breastfeeding promotion, micronutrient supplementation, growth monitoring, deworming, and nutrition counseling. Additionally, local government units have their own community nutrition and food security initiatives. One of the most successful was implemented in Quezon Province when now-Congressman Jay Suarez was governor. Quezon Province was one of the pioneers in implementing the First 1,000 Days program, feeding the baby even while still in the womb of the mother.

Because of the magnitude of this problem of child stunting due to undernutrition, the private sector must do its share in ensuring that vulnerable children receive adequate nourishment during their critical years of growth and learning. That is why the Philippine Food Bank Foundation decided to partner with a public school in Muntinlupa in a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) program called “Balik Lusog.”

It was launched at Poblacion Elementary School in Muntinlupa in partnership with the Loaves and Fish Foundation, made possible by a generous grant from the Starbucks Foundation. The children that the program set out to feed were 500 learners from Grades 3 to 6—children identified as malnourished or undernourished. Many of them come from families relocated from the railroad tracks. They were coming to school on empty stomachs, and because they were hungry, it was very difficult for them to learn.

For 38 school days—from Jan. 26 to March 19, 2026—the Loaves and Fish kitchen cooked fresh, nutritious meals every single morning. Parent volunteers from a private school, PAREF Southridge, delivered the meals to the school. Teachers and the school nurse watched over every child every single school day. At the end of those 38 days, the children were subjected to health measurements: ninety-five percent (95 percent) of the 500 children gained weight. Furthermore, every subject—English, Filipino, Science, Mathematics, and Araling Panlipunan—showed higher test scores in the fourth quarter than in the quarter prior to when the feeding started.

Children who used to arrive tired and distracted became more alert. Children with frequent absences started showing up daily—because for some of them, the meal served in school was the only decent meal for the whole day. One child told a teacher, “I am excited to come to school now.” That child, fed, healthy, and learning today, is the nurse, the engineer, the teacher, or the entrepreneur of tomorrow. The Philippine Food Bank spent just 57 centavos per meal to invest in the human resources of tomorrow, thanks to the donation of surplus food, dedicated volunteers, and the quiet faith of sponsors who agreed to help even before they knew the outcome.

Fortunately, the Starbucks Foundation has generously invited the Philippine Food Bank to apply for a second grant. The officials, with the support of numerous donors—among them those who participated in the Golf Tournament at Tagaytay Midlands—have every intention of going beyond one grant and one school. The Balik Lusog program resumed at Poblacion Elementary School in Muntinlupa on July 27, 2026, the exact same day that President Marcos delivered his SONA. Close to 1,000 undernourished children in Grades two to six will once again be fed for as many days as possible during the school year.

From there, the Foundation plans to bring Balik Lusog to every public elementary school in Muntinlupa, hopefully in partnership with the School-Based Feeding Program of the Department of Education. The Foundation is now in conversations with officials from the Department of Education so that a formal Public-Private Partnership framework can be developed on the basis of our experience at the elementary school in Muntinlupa. Our next target is the City of Pasig, where two leading government officials, Mayor Vico Sotto and Congressman Roman Romulo, are among the most enlightened on this long-festering problem of child undernutrition and its very deleterious effect on the quality of our human resources.

After the Foundation perfects the Muntinlupa and Pasig models, there is no limit to what can be accomplished across the numerous Philippine municipalities. We hope the Balik Lusog experiment in Muntinlupa can inspire other private initiatives combating hunger in the Philippines to adopt the PPP model, ensuring government funds are best utilized with a minimum of inefficiency and poor governance.

I am especially referring to several notable private initiatives. Among corporate foundation feeding programs, many large Philippine enterprises operate long-term nutrition programs through their foundations, including the Jollibee Group Foundation (Busog, Lusog, Talino—BLT—feeding program and community kitchens), Pilipinas Shell Foundation (school-community nutrition projects), Ayala Foundation (nutrition and maternal-child health initiatives), Aboitiz Foundation (community feeding and nutrition education), Metrobank Foundation (support for nutrition and health programs), Manila Water Foundation (nutrition linked to clean water and sanitation), ABS-CBN Lingkod Kapamilya Foundation (feeding and nutrition assistance), and GMA Kapuso Foundation (nutrition and disaster feeding).

Faith-based organizations also play a vital role, including Caritas Philippines, Feed the Hungry Philippines, various Catholic diocesan feeding programs, and several Protestant and Evangelical feeding groups. Similarly, NGO-led nutrition programs contribute immensely to the cause, such as the Philippine Food Bank Foundation, Rise Against Hunger, Project PEARLS, Kabisig ng Kalahi, Gawad Kalinga, and the NVC Foundation, whose Mingo nutrition program provides fortified complementary food to undernourished children.

I have by no means prepared an exhaustive list of private initiatives that directly address the serious problem of undernourished children. In fact, it can be arguably stated that the Philippines has one of Southeast Asia’s broadest networks of private-sector nutrition initiatives. Corporate foundations, NGOs, churches, civic organizations, and international partners collectively invest hundreds of millions of pesos each year in feeding programs, nutrition, food fortification, community kitchens, breastfeeding promotion, and livelihood initiatives.

title: Context-specific climate policies highlighted in Climate Resilience Forum
content_lead:
THE Climate Change Commission (CCC) on Thursday stressed the need to provide a blueprint for context-specific climate-resilient policies at the 2026 National Climate Resilience Forum.

The forum, held on Thursday in Taguig City, convened local leaders to advance the National Adaptation Plan which outlines how a country will adapt to the long-term climate impacts.

"National frameworks provide a coherent road map for enhancing climate resilience as we pursue low-carbon development. However, we know that policies on paper cannot protect a community from a storm, and it is only through decisive action on the ground," said CCC Commissioner Rachel Anne Herrera.

To achieve this requires risk-sensitive and localized planning to address specific vulnerabilities, Herrera said.

Robert Borje, CCC vice chairman and executive director, said adaptation "can't remain an aspiration of any group; it must become visible in safer schools and cities, stronger infrastructure, protected coastlines, climate-smart agriculture and forward local governance." Cavite 8th District Rep. Aniela Bianca Tolentino, who chairs the House Committee on Climate Change, said legislation continues to play a crucial role in fostering climate resilience.

"Over the past months, our committee has been actively deliberating measures that seek to strengthen the country's climate governance and accelerate the transition toward a resilient and low-carbon economy," said Tolentino.

She outlined several proposed laws, including the Low-Carbon Economy Investment Act to support clean technologies, and the Climate Accountability Act to modernize governance frameworks.

She also emphasized the importance of ensuring that climate financing reaches local government units (LGUs), the frontline responders to climate risks.

title: Promises, performance, and the 'mahiya naman kayo' moment
content_lead:
As we prepare to listen to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s State of the Nation Address this afternoon, it is only fitting to look back at what was promised -- and what has been delivered -- since the 2025 SONA. Last year's address was defined by bold commitments: ₱20 rice, zero-balance billing in hospitals, lifeline electricity rates, and expanded support for small businesses. Today, as we evaluate the administration's progress, the measure of this SONA will not be found in applause lines, but in whether performance has caught up with promise.

When President Marcos Jr. delivered his 2025 State of the Nation Address, he chose to speak less of promises and more of performance. It was a deliberate pivot: a leader entering the final stretch of his term, conscious that history will judge him not by rhetoric but by delivery.

However, the numbers in 2026 tell a more complex story than the optimism of a year ago. While the 2025 address offered hope, the current economic landscape faces significant headwinds. Inflation, which had tempered to 1.4 percent by June 2025, has proven stubborn, rising to 6.4 percent in June 2026. This remains consistently above the central bank's 2-4 percent target, keeping the cost of living high for ordinary families. Furthermore, core inflation -- which strips away volatile items -- reached 4.4 percent in June, the highest in 31 months, signaling that price pressures have become broad-based.

The administration's record remains a mixed bag. Out of more than 160 commitments, roughly one in four have been fulfilled. While the Maharlika Investment Fund moved from concept to reality and flagship projects like the Panguil Bay Bridge and the LRT-1 Cavite Extension gave substance to the "Build Better More" mantra, infrastructure momentum has slowed. In the first quarter of 2026, public construction saw a sharp 31.5 percent year-on-year contraction as various projects faced delays.

l'essentiel Après six années de travail, l'ANA-CEN Ariège est devenue propriétaire de l'entrée de la grotte de Tourtouse, en Ariège. Une acquisition stratégique pour préserver ce site naturel majeur, refuge de plus de 6 000 chauves-souris en été.

Après six années de travail, l'ANA-CEN Ariège est devenue propriétaire de l'entrée de la grotte de Tourtouse, en Ariège, le 9 juillet 2026. Une acquisition qui doit permettre de renforcer la protection de ce site reconnu depuis longtemps pour son patrimoine naturel et scientifique.

Située à proximité du village, la grotte de Tourtouse a été explorée par de nombreux chercheurs depuis la fin du XIX siècle. L'abbé Pouech s'y est notamment intéressé pour l'archéologie, avant que le laboratoire souterrain de Moulis et son directeur Albert Vandel n'y étudient la faune invertébrée. Aujourd'hui, l'attention se porte particulièrement sur les chauves-souris qui y trouvent un refuge majeur.

Un site confronté à "un contexte foncier morcelé"

La richesse du site a conduit à son intégration dans plusieurs dispositifs de protection. Un arrêté préfectoral de protection de biotope interdit "toute modification du milieu" et encadre les visites afin de préserver les populations de chauves-souris, précise l'ANA-CEN dans un communiqué. La grotte est également intégrée à un site Natura 2000, permettant leur suivi et la mise en place d'aides pour les forestiers et agriculteurs volontaires. Un projet de Réserve naturelle nationale porté par l'État vise également à assurer "la protection forte d'un réseau de sites souterrains sur le département".

title: In Manila's shadow, a forest refuge still shelters rare plants
content_lead:
A mountainous reserve near Manila, the Philippine capital, is a critical ecological refuge, harboring high levels of plant diversity despite its proximity to the highly urbanized city, according to a recent study.

The findings come from surveys done 10 years earlier, however, and mounting pressures on the area's forests since then may have had an impact, the authors say.

As the last remaining natural lowland forest in Cavite province, on the southern shores of Manila Bay, Mounts Palay-palay-Mataas-na-Gulod Protected Landscape serves as a vital stronghold for Philippine biodiversity, researchers say.

In July 2016, they surveyed plants within the landscape, known as MPPMGPL. At the time, they documented 294 species of plants across the landscape's varied habitats, from grasslands and secondary forests to old-growth stands. They found that 42 species, or 16%, are found only in the Philippines, while 31 species are classified as threatened on national or international red lists.

"The most remarkable finding is that this landscape ... harbors an incredibly high concentration of biodiversity despite being so close to highly urbanized zones," study lead author Enrico Replan, an assistant professor at the Institute of Environmental Science and Meteorology (IESM) at the University of the Philippines Diliman, told Mongabay by email.

The study also identified 43 species that likely represent new records for Cavite province, "filling major geographic knowledge gaps," Replan said. Among the most significant findings was the dominance of guijo (Shorea guiso), a critically endangered tree species, in the forest's interior core. This highlights the role of MPPMGPL as a key conservation refuge, the authors write.

While the study was only published recently, Replan told Mongabay the 2016 findings offer a baseline for this landscape; there haven't been similar surveys since.

title: Cavite under state of calamity due to effects of 'Luis,' 'Maymay'
content_lead:
Cavite has been placed under a state of calamity after heavy rains from the southwest monsoon, intensified by tropical cyclones "Luis" and "Maymay," caused widespread damage.

The Provincial Board approved Resolution No. 5059-2026 during its regular session on Aug. 10.

The resolution authorized Gov. Francisco Gabriel "Abeng" D. Remulla to use P10 million from the Quick Response Fund of the 2026 Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund to respond to the calamity.

Based on situation reports received by the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (PDRRMC), 20 local government units (LGUs) were affected by heavy rains and flooding, involving 10,469 families or 34,952 individuals.

Authorities also recorded 97 incidents, including flooding, toppled or fallen trees, landslides or soil erosion, collapsed structures, fires, and vehicular accidents.

The initial damage to agriculture, meanwhile, was estimated at P4.23 million.

In a Facebook post, Remulla said the provincial government continues to monitor situations in various LGUs and provide assistance to residents who need it.

He also urged his constituents to remain alert, keep abreast of official advisories, and prioritize their families' safety.
relevance_summary: Relevant to food insecurity via General food-insecurity relevance. Signals: agricultural production, crop losses disaster. Location: Cavite.

title: Joy Barcoma, nanawagan sa responsableng pagtatapon ng basura
content_lead:
May panawagan si The People Have Spoken celebri-peep Joy Barcoma kaugnay sa kasalukuyang pagbaha sa Pilipinas.

Nitong Miyerkules (August 12), bumisita ang beauty queen-advocate sa clean-up drive sa Kasiglahan Village, Rodriguez, Rizal.

Kasama si Baus Rufo para sa Unang Hirit, namahagi ng munting sorpresa ang duo sa mga tao habang ipinakita ang kasalukuyang lagay ng mga daan matapos ang pagbaha.

"Bakas pa rin po ang pinsala na dulot po ng habagat. Pero kung makikita n'yo, pare-parehas pa rin po ang problema ng mga residente at maging ng ibang lugar na binaha," ani Joy sa isang video sa kanyang social media.

READ: Joy Barcoma urges Pinoys to make better choices in 2028 amid widespread flooding

Maya-maya pa, itinuro ng "pambansang jusa" ang mga basurang naiwan at nakakalat sa lugar dahil sa hindi wastong pagtatapon ng mga ito.

"Panawagan po ito, hindi lang po sa mga barangay [at] gobyerno, kundi maging sa lahat ng tao na maging mas responsable po tayo sa mga tinatapon nating basura. Dahil kung ano'ng tinapon mong basura ngayon, 'yun ang babalik sa'yo sa susunod na panahon," dagdag niya.

Noong Lunes (August 10), ipinakita rin ng UH host mate ang kondisyon ng isang evacuation center sa Cavite.

"Supposedly po ay dapat ligtas na lugar po para sa atin mga kababayan. Pero kung makikita n'yo kahit evacuation center ho natin ay binabaha." aniya.

"So sana ho ayusin na ho natin ang mga desisyon natin sa 2028 para hindi na po nakakaranas ng ganitong klaseng inconvenience 'yung mga kababayan ho natin na nakakaranas po ng pagbaha at siyempre pangangailangan lumikas sa panahon po ng habagat o ng bagyo at tuloy-tuloy na pag-ulan."

title: Hiking at Mount Pico de Loro suspended for rehab due to Habagat, cyclones
content_lead:
The hiking activities at Mount Pico de Loro and the Mounts Palay-Palay/Mataas-na-Gulod Protected Landscape (MPPMNGPL) are suspended from August 21 to September 12 for rehabilitation after some areas were damaged due to the monsoon rains and the recent tropical cyclones, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) said on Thursday.

"Ipinagbibigay-alam sa publiko na ang lahat ng hiking activities sa Mt. Pico de Loro/ MPPMNGPL ay pansamantalang sususpindihin mula Agosto 21, 2026 - Setyembre 12, 2026, upang bigyang-daan ang paglilinis, pagsasaayos, at rehabilitasyon ng mga napinsalang bahagi ng pinangangalagaang pook dulot ng nagdaang bagyo at habagat," the advisory read.

(The public is informed that all hiking activities at Mt. Pico de Loro/MPPMNGPL will be temporarily suspended from August 21, 2026 - September 12, 2026, to pave the way for the clearing, repair, and rehabilitation of damaged areas in the protected landscape caused by recent storms and the Habagat.)

The DENR said that it will conduct inspection and maintenance of hiking trails, clearing of fallen trees and other obstructions, as well as other necessary measures for the safety of the hikers.

"Hinihiling namin ang inyong pang-unawa at pakikiisa sa pansamantalang hakbang na ito," the department said.

(We ask for your understanding and cooperation regarding this temporary measure.)

The Mount Pico de Loro is part of the 3,972-hectare MPPMNGPL, along with other peaks: Palay-palay and Mataas-na-Gulod.

Pico de Loro was named for its summit that resembles a parrot's beak. It is also the highest mountain in Cavite at 2,257 feet.

It reopened to the public in January 2023 after six years of rehabilitation. -- LDF, GMA News

title: Victory! Illegal Horse Race Cancelled In Laguna After PETA Push | Journal Online
content_lead:
Manila -- In a groundbreaking victory for horses, authorities in Liliw, Laguna, have cancelled an illegal horse race that was scheduled to take place on 25 July -- taking action within 24 hours after PETA alerted them that the event would expose horses to significant risks of injury, exhaustion, and stress. This marks the first time in the country that authorities have successfully stopped an illegal horse race before it could take place.

In its letter to Mayor Ildefonso Monleon, PETA noted that the event -- which was planned as part of fiesta celebration at a barangay in Liliw -- would likely violate the Animal Welfare Act and was being conducted outside the regulatory authority of the Philippine Racing Commission. PETA also contacted several government agencies -- including the Bureau of Animal Industry, the Municipal Agriculture, and the Philippine National Police local offices in Liliw -- and the authorities acted swiftly to cancel the race.

"This is a historic moment for horses in the Philippines and shows what can be achieved when authorities prioritize animal welfare," says PETA President Jason Baker. "PETA urges other local governments across the country to follow Liliw's compassionate example and prevent dangerous horse races from taking place in their jurisdictions."

Horses used for racing are forced to sprint at speeds so fast that they frequently sustain catastrophic and often fatal injuries. When they stop winning races, many horses are killed.

PETA -- whose motto reads, in part, that "animals are not ours to use for entertainment" -- points out that when it comes to the ability to feel pain, hunger, and fear, a horse is a dog is a boy. LOS BAÑOS, Laguna -- The Southeast Asian Regional Center for Graduate Study and Research in Agriculture (Searca) will lead the development of a regional micro-credential curriculum on regenerative and resilient agriculture in collaboration with two other centers under the Southeast Asian Ministers of Education Organization (Seameo).

title: Drones help develop better rice varieties

FOR years, making better rice meant scientists walking fields with clipboards and testing plants one by one. Now, researchers at the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) are doing much of that work from the sky -- and in the lab.

In a study published in Current Plant Biology, IRRI scientists used drones and genetic testing to find rice varieties that can turn sunlight into grain more efficiently. The goal is simple: grow more rice on the same land, even as the climate gets hotter and less predictable.

Why this matters

By 2050, the world will need about 50 percent more rice and other grains to feed a growing population. But rice yields are only increasing by less than 1 percent each year.

title: PLDT, Smart help MSMEs build digital skills for business growth
content_lead:
PLDT and Smart Communications brought digital learning sessions to 21 communities across the Philippines during the first half of 2026, reaching 1,279 MSMEs, agripreneurs, tourism stakeholders, and livelihood beneficiaries.

The workshops were conducted with partners including the Department of Trade and Industry, Department of Social Welfare and Development, International Trade Centre Digital-PINAS initiative, and local government units. Sessions covered digital entrepreneurship, content creation, online marketing, product presentation, smartphone photography, and cybersecurity awareness.

Helping local enterprises reach more customers

For Queen G. Anino, a rice producer from Santa Cruz, Laguna, the training came as she was beginning to build an online presence for Cabisera Rice.

"The training came at the right time because we are just starting to promote Cabisera Rice and are only beginning to build our social media presence," Anino said. "With these tools and modern methods, we are excited to become farmer-entrepreneurs who can actively market our products."

title: Searca highlights climate-resilient farming, promising ube varieties
content_lead:
LOS BAÑOS, Laguna -- Long prized as a staple in Filipino culinary tradition, purple yam -- locally known as ube -- is emerging as a key driver of agricultural growth and climate resilience for smallholder farmers.

Insights featured in the Agriculture and Development Seminar Series (ADSS) organized by the Southeast Asian Regional Center for Graduate Study and Research in Agriculture (Searca) show that while global and domestic demand for ube continues to surge, local supply struggles to keep pace, creating a significant opportunity to transform traditional root-crop farming into a highly profitable enterprise.

Market demand remains strong, with ube exports generating $3.06 million in 2025 through sought-after processed products such as powders, purees, and traditional pastes (halaya).

However, domestic production reached only about 13,535 metric tons in 2022, compared with a national demand of 49,000 metric tons. Low baseline yields, seasonal crop behavior, tuber dormancy, and a shortage of quality planting materials continue to limit overall production.

To bridge this gap, agricultural frameworks under the High Value Crops Development Program (HVCDP) of the Department of Agriculture (DA) are prioritizing crop resilience and diversification.

title: El área Recreativa de La Laguna en Valleseco ofrece un verano de aprendizaje y diversión a 120 niños
content_lead:
Desde hace cerca de dos décadas el Área Recreativa y las instalaciones deportivas municipales de La Laguna en Valleseco acoge el campus de verano para los más pequeños. Un espacio en el que 120 niños y niñas aprenden acerca del ecosistema, para fomentar así unas vacaciones alejadas de la tecnología. Cada jornada combina estas experiencias con actividades deportivas, juegos, talleres, piscina, rutas por la naturaleza y dinámicas al aire libre.

El curso de verano busca que los participantes aprendan lecciones mientras acarician un animal, riegan una planta recién sembrada o comparten una mañana de juegos en plena naturaleza. El objetivo es que los niños se alejen de las pantallas mientras aprenden y juegan acerca de la riqueza del sector primario a la vez que crean nuevas amistades. El campus pondrá fin a las actividades el 31 de agosto, aunque los niños y niñas llevan disfrutando de las jornadas desde el pasado uno de julio.

Los niños y niñas que participan en estas jornadas pueden desde dar de comer a animales como cabras, ovejas, gallinas y burros de la granja hasta cuidar y ver como crecen las hortalizas que han sembrado durante el verano. De esta manera, el campus fomenta el trabajo en la tierra con calabacines, habichuelas, lechugas o col rizada para que los más pequeños valoren el esfuerzo que realizan los agricultores desde plantar el cultivo hasta cuando llega a la mesa.

También cuentan con actividades como aprender nuevos insectos, construir pequeñas casetas en el bosque o saber cuál es la forma adecuada de proteger a la naturaleza. El campus no solo se centra en el municipio de Valleseco, sino que los niños y niñas podrán disfrutar de varias salidas durante su duración, entre ellas la playa de Las Alcaravaneras, ir a ver una película al cine, visitar el Cenobio de Valerón, conocer más de 550 especies de animales en el acuario Poema del Mar o disfrutar del recreativo Ilusiona en el centro comercial Los Alisios.

Ksamil es un pequeño pueblo costero situado en el extremo sur de Albania, a unos 17 kilómetros de Saranda. En pocos años ha pasado de ser un rincón casi desconocido a convertirse en uno de los mejores destinos de playa de toda Europa, gracias a sus aguas cristalina y un paisaje que recuerda sorprendentemente a las playas de Ibiza. Uno de sus grandes atractivos son las cuatro pequeñas islas que se encuentran frente a la costa.

Ksamil forma parte del Parque Nacional de Butrinto, declarado Patrimonio de la Humanidad por la UNESCO, y su privilegiada ubicación permite combinar días de playa con visitas a uno de los yacimientos arqueológicos más importantes de los Balcanes, rodeado de bosques, lagunas y una naturaleza espectacular. Aunque el pueblo nació durante la época comunista como un pequeño asentamiento agrícola, el turismo ha transformado por completo la zona en la última década. Aun así, sigue conservando un ambiente mucho más tranquilo que otros destinos del Mediterráneo.

La Rivera Albanesa, un paraíso de sol y playa

Antes de convertirse en uno de los destinos más populares de la Riviera Albanesa, Ksamil era poco más que un tramo de costa salvaje. Hasta mediados del siglo XX solo había colinas, pequeñas bahías vírgenes y algún rebaño de cabras y ovejas disfrutando del paisaje. No fue hasta 1966, durante la etapa comunista, cuando el gobierno decidió fundar un nuevo pueblo con un doble objetivo: impulsar la agricultura y desarrollar el turismo.

Su nombre también tiene historia. Ksamil deriva del griego Examilia, que significa "seis millas", la distancia aproximada que separa este rincón de Albania de la isla griega de Corfú. La que pudo ser una de las ciudades más bellas del mundo olvidó sus aguas, sus quebradas, sus lagunas (como la de San Mateo o la Laguna de los Caracoles, que también desaparecieron; que fue cubierta y maldita por un cura, donde "abrevaron" y se "sustentaron" los soldados de Alfinger). El pronóstico del tiempo para Laguna Brava este lunes 20 de julio indica que la temperatura máxima será de -5°C y la mínima de -8°C.

A su vez, de acuerdo con el Servicio Meteorológico Nacional (SMN), se estiman vientos de 53 km/h, y la humedad promedio será del 69%.

El reporte del SMN informa que en las primeras horas de este lunes 20 de julio se esperan lluvias intensas de 18 mm, la humedad será del 69% y se esperan vientos fuertes de 53 km/h del noroeste.

En tanto, para la media mañana se esperan precipitaciones ligeras de 3 mm, la humedad será del 63% y habrá vientos fuertes de 50 km/h del noroeste.

Según el pronóstico del organismo en Laguna Brava, para esta tarde se anuncia una lluvia moderada de 6 mm y se esperan vientos fuertes de 42 km/h del noroeste.

En tanto, para esta noche, se anticipa una precipitación moderada de 14 mm y habrá vientos moderados de 34 km/h del noroeste.

El Servicio Meteorológico Nacional (SMN) es el organismo oficial encargado de recopilar, analizar y difundir información meteorológica en el país. Su función principal es predecir el clima y el tiempo atmosférico, emitir alertas tempranas sobre fenómenos meteorológicos peligrosos y brindar información climática para diversas actividades, como la aviación, la agricultura y la navegación.

El SMN opera a través de una red de estaciones meteorológicas distribuidas por todo el país, además de utilizar imágenes satelitales y modelos de predicción numérica.

El próximo 30 de julio, Edu Torres tomará los fogones de Mar de Sazzon, el restaurante del complejo Laguna Beach en Estepona (Playa Padrón). Lo hará en dos turnos, a las 13.30 y a las 15.30 horas, con un menú cerrado que ya está disponible bajo reserva.

El precio arranca en 42€ por persona. Incluye tres entrantes (salchichón de cabra, aguacate relleno de atún rojo y carpaccio al ajillo) y dos arroces firmados por el cocinero. El primero, de chuletita de cordero y sus riñones. El segundo, el Arroz Clandestino 2026. Una receta que él mismo define como secreta y que forma parte de su repertorio más personal.

Torres no es un cocinero al uso. Detrás de él está Molino Roca, una firma familiar que trabaja el arroz desde 1903. Pero su enfoque ha ido más allá del producto: ha convertido la paella en un vehículo divulgativo. Participa en realities, documentales y eventos internacionales. Ha cocinado en Quito, Turquía, Argentina, Eslovenia, Italia y, sobre todo, en ciudades de Estados Unidos como Atlanta o Nueva York.

Su discurso insiste en que la paella no es un plato para impresionar, sino para reunir.

"La paella no se cocina para impresionar; se cocina para reunir a las personas alrededor del fuego y crear recuerdos para toda la vida", sostiene.

Y en esa línea, el menú de Mar de Sazzon es un homenaje a los encuentros que organiza cada año en la Albufera de Valencia con arroceros, agricultores y chefs con estrella Michelin.

La colaboración es uno de los eventos centrales del verano en Laguna Beach, el complejo de Rosauro Varo que aglutina varios espacios: Kai Beach (beach club de inspiración asiática), Sublim (piscina infinita y ambiente vibrante) y el propio Mar de Sazzon, centrado en cocina española y andaluza con producto de proximidad. title: Las mujeres que desafían la Laguna Merín para sostener un oficio de toda la vida
content_lead:
Como es tradicional desde hace décadas, la pesca artesanal en la Laguna Merín ha sido una actividad sostenida por familias enteras. Aunque el oficio suele asociarse a los hombres, detrás de cada embarcación también hay mujeres que arman redes, navegan, procesan el pescado y participan de cada etapa de la cadena productiva. Ahora, un grupo de seis pescadoras del pueblo Laguna Merín, en el departamento de Cerro Largo, obtuvo un respaldo económico que les permitirá fortalecer su trabajo y mejorar las condiciones en las que elaboran sus productos.

El Colectivo de Mujeres de la Pesca Artesanal de la Laguna Merín resultó ser uno de los 23 seleccionados en la sexta edición de Transformadoras, la convocatoria de Políticas Afirmativas para Mujeres Rurales impulsada por el Ministerio de Ganadería, Agricultura y Pesca (MGAP) y el Instituto Plan Agropecuario. La iniciativa distribuirá $ 3.800.000 entre proyectos colectivos de todo el país y, en este caso, destinará $ 180.000 al grupo integrado por Rafaela Carnales, Mónica Collazo, Carla González, María Porciúncula, Marisa García y Verónica Larrosa.

La convocatoria forma parte de la Política de Género Agro, una estrategia cuyo plan para el período 2025-2029 contempla 40 medidas orientadas a reducir las brechas de género en el ámbito agropecuario.

Para Rafaela Carnales, de 20 años, el proyecto representa la posibilidad de consolidar una forma de trabajo que lleva décadas desarrollándose de manera casi invisible. title: Pesca, un 'Piano Marshall' per salvare le imprese: "Serve un programma straordinario di investimenti"
content_lead:
La proposta è stata lanciata a Chioggia nel corso dell'incontro "Mediterraneo che bolle e crisi vongole"

PORTO TOLLE (ROVIGO) - Il Commissario straordinario non basta più. Prima il granchio blu. Poi le macroalghe. Infine, la moria di cozze, provocata da un'acqua che nella laguna di Scardovari ha raggiunto i 32 gradi. Il comparto ittico dell'Alto Adriatico si trova oggi ad affrontare una crisi che non è più soltanto ambientale, ma economica e produttiva. Per questo dal mondo della cooperazione arriva una proposta destinata ad aprire il dibattito: un "Piano Marshall" per l'Alto Adriatico: un programma straordinario di investimenti per salvare le imprese della pesca e accompagnare il settore verso un futuro profondamente segnato dai cambiamenti climatici.

La proposta è stata lanciata a Chioggia nel corso dell'incontro "Mediterraneo che bolle e crisi vongole", promosso da Legacoop Agroalimentare nella sede del Consorzio di gestione della pesca dei molluschi bivalvi (Cogevo). Al tavolo erano presenti il sottosegretario al Ministero dell'Agricoltura, della Sovranità alimentare e delle Foreste, Patrizio Giacomo La Pietra, la direttrice generale del ministero Graziella Romito, il dirigente della Regione, Giuseppe Cherubini e i rappresentanti delle cooperative, delle organizzazioni di produttori e dei consorzi dell'Alto Adriatico.

L'incontro arriva dopo settimane particolarmente difficili per il comparto. Nella Sacca di Scardovari gli allevatori hanno infatti subito una pesante moria di cozze causata dalle temperature eccezionalmente elevate dell'acqua. Un'emergenza che si aggiunge ai danni provocati dal granchio blu e agli squilibri ambientali determinati dalla proliferazione delle macroalghe, confermando come il riscaldamento del mare stia modificando profondamente gli equilibri dell'acquacoltura.

title: La Laguna: productores y lecheros no logran acuerdo sobre precios

En La Laguna, productores y lecheros no logran acuerdo sobre precios. | Rolando Riestra.

A puerta cerrada y sin acceso a los medios, más de tres horas invirtieron las agrupaciones de productores y empresarios lecheros en la búsqueda de un mejor precio para las cosechas de forraje de sorgo y maíz; sin embargo, el resultado fue el mismo: no hubo acuerdo.

Las oficinas de la Delegación de la Secretaría de Agricultura y Desarrollo Rural (SADER) en Lerdo fueron cerradas con elementos de vigilancia para impedir el acceso de los medios al encuentro, al que no acudieron los representantes de los gobiernos estatales de Durango y Coahuila, lo que, según los productores, reflejó apatía, desatención y falta de voluntad para atender esta problemática.

Te recomendamos...

Este ciclo agrícola, según datos oficiales de la propia SADER, se sembraron en La Laguna 32 mil hectáreas de maíz, así como 14 mil de sorgo, siendo los cultivos predominantes de la zona agrícola que abarca los estados de Coahuila y Durango.

Productores exponen afectaciones

Samuel Martínez González, dirigente de la Confederación Nacional Campesina en Lerdo, sostuvo que al final de poco o nada sirvieron los argumentos expuestos, ya que no hubo un acuerdo favorable a su propuesta de obtener un subsidio de 20 centavos por kilo de forraje de maíz y sorgo vendido para equilibrar los costos, como tampoco existió voluntad de los estableros para mejorar su oferta en la compra de las cosechas.

title: Ramón Navia, agricultor: "No es el agua, son los fertilizantes con nitrato lo que contamina el acuífero y el mar
content_lead:
Se requieren medidas como la reducción real de fertilizantes, control de regadíos ilegales y restauración de humedales para revertir la situación.

El Mar Menor no se volvió verde por una sola causa, ni se explica con una frase simple. Pero hay una idea que varios técnicos y científicos repiten desde hace años: el problema no es solo el agua, sino lo que arrastra.

Ramón Navia, ingeniero agrónomo, lo expresó con claridad en Onda Cero: "No es el agua, es el nitrato lo que contamina el acuífero y el Mar Menor". Su frase apunta al corazón del conflicto ambiental murciano.

La tesis es incómoda porque desplaza el foco. No basta con discutir de dónde viene el agua, si del trasvase, de pozos, de desaladoras o de lluvias. La pregunta decisiva es qué lleva dentro.

Los nitratos son muy solubles. Esa cualidad los hace útiles para alimentar cultivos, pero también peligrosos cuando se aplican en exceso. Si la planta no los absorbe, el riego o la lluvia pueden lavarlos hacia el subsuelo.

Ahí empieza el problema del acuífero. Durante décadas, parte del nitrógeno usado en la agricultura intensiva del Campo de Cartagena se ha filtrado hacia capas profundas y ha dejado una carga contaminante difícil de eliminar.

Crecen microalgas y el agua se enturbia

El Mar Menor recibe esos nutrientes por varias vías: escorrentías, ramblas, drenajes, aportes subterráneos y lluvias intensas. Cuando llegan demasiados nitratos y fosfatos, la laguna se desequilibra y aparece la eutrofización.

La eutrofización parece, al principio, un exceso de vida. Crecen microalgas, el agua se enturbia, llega menos luz al fondo y las praderas marinas se debilitan. Después, la descomposición consume oxígeno y puede provocar mortandades.

Eso convirtió al Mar Menor en símbolo. La "sopa verde", los peces muertos, la pérdida de transparencia y el deterioro de sus fondos mostraron al público un proceso que llevaba años gestándose en tierra.

title: Alofite, le piante che nascono dal sale: la Laguna di Venezia nel progetto europeo per l'agricoltura del futuro | Il Giornale dei Marinai
content_lead:
L'aumento delle temperature, la scarsità crescente di acqua dolce e la progressiva salinizzazione dei suoli stanno mettendo sotto pressione l'agricoltura in tutto il bacino del Mediterraneo. Le zone umide costiere -- lagune, saline, delta fluviali -- sono tra gli ambienti più esposti: qui l'acqua di mare risale nelle falde e nei terreni agricoli, rendendo sempre più difficile coltivare le specie tradizionali.

È in questo scenario che si inserisce HALO-FORCE (Halophyte-Driven Innovation for Sustainable Farming in Mediterranean Wetlands), progetto quadriennale finanziato nell'ambito di PRIMA -- Partnership for Research and Innovation in the Mediterranean Area, cofinanziato dall'Unione Europea, e coordinato dall'Università degli Studi di Padova.

Perché la Laguna di Venezia

Il sistema lagunare veneziano è stato scelto come uno dei quattro siti sperimentali del progetto, insieme a Sidi Boughaba (Marocco), Burg el Arab (Egitto) e la zona umida di Alaçatı (Turchia) -- un campione che copre gran parte della variabilità climatica e ambientale del Mediterraneo.

Il lavoro sul campo, condotto da CORILA (il consorzio interuniversitario che coordina la ricerca sulla Laguna) insieme all'Università di Padova, è già cominciato: si stanno individuando le future aree di prelievo dei semi all'interno del sistema lagunare, un primo passo per mappare gli habitat delle popolazioni selvatiche di alofite e raccogliere i dati necessari alla realizzazione di un vivaio dedicato.

Pierpaolo Campostrini, direttore generale di CORILA, sottolinea come la Laguna sia un contesto scientificamente prezioso proprio perché ospita da sempre piante spontanee commestibili adattate agli ambienti salini. Con l'avanzare della salinizzazione dei suoli in molte aree costiere del Mediterraneo -- spinta dal cambiamento climatico e dall'intrusione del cuneo salino -- la conoscenza già maturata in Laguna può offrire indicazioni utili a territori che si trovano ad affrontare lo stesso problema solo adesso.

title: Laguna de Zumpango: una segunda oportunidad para aprender
content_lead:
Hace poco más de dos años escribía en este espacio una pregunta que resumía el fracaso de nuestra política hídrica: ¿Quién secó la Laguna de Zumpango? En aquel momento sólo quedaban tierra agrietada, incendios y la incertidumbre de cientos de familias que veían desaparecer el último gran vaso lacustre del Valle de México.

Meses después llegaron lluvias extraordinarias que la llevaron incluso a superar su capacidad de almacenamiento. Luego apareció otra amenaza: una invasión masiva de lirio acuático cubrió casi en su totalidad su superficie y volvió a evidenciar el deterioro ambiental del ecosistema. En muy poco tiempo, Zumpango pasó de la sequía extrema a la abundancia y de ésta a una nueva crisis. Quizá ningún otro cuerpo de agua refleja con tanta claridad la fragilidad de la gestión hídrica en México.

Hoy el Gobierno Federal propone escribir un capítulo distinto. Con una inversión superior a los 10 mil 500 millones de pesos, impulsa un proyecto para recuperar la laguna y convertirla nuevamente en un activo estratégico para el Valle de México.

La iniciativa contempla desazolvar el vaso, rehabilitar bordos, construir plantas de tratamiento y potabilización, instalar estaciones de bombeo y nuevos acueductos para incorporar el agua al abastecimiento de la Zona Metropolitana, además de restaurar parte de sus funciones ambientales. Si las metas se cumplen, Zumpango volvería a ser, al mismo tiempo, un humedal vivo y una fuente adicional de agua para millones de personas.

Sería mezquino negar el alcance de esta apuesta. Diversificar las fuentes de abastecimiento, disminuir la presión sobre acuíferos sobreexplotados y recuperar un ecosistema degradado son objetivos que cualquier política pública debería perseguir. Después de décadas viendo desaparecer cuerpos de agua, resulta alentador que el Estado vuelva la mirada hacia uno de los más emblemáticos.

Pero tampoco sería responsable celebrar antes de tiempo.
