La iniciativa se ha visto marcada por la controversia, pues Karkosik ha anunciado recientemente despidos colectivos que afectarán a unas 200 personas (casi la mitad de la plantilla) en su fábrica de metales.

Los creadores del proyecto son el escultor Adam Jakub Matejkowski y el diseñador Aleksander Skórski, quienes declararon que el objetivo trasciende lo monumental y su importancia "no se basa solamente en tener dimensiones récord, sino en su capacidad de atracción para convertirse en un lugar de oración, reflexión y peregrinación".

Por su parte, las autoridades municipales y los residentes confían en que el monumento sirva para activar pequeños negocios y servicios en una zona que hasta ahora ha tenido un perfil predominantemente rural y agrícola.

title: Delivery rider struck by toppled tree, post in Antipolo
content_lead:
A delivery rider who was taking shelter along Circumferential Road in Barangay San Roque, Antipolo City, was brought to the hospital after being struck when a tree and post toppled on Sunday, Aug. 9, amid continued rains brought by the southwest monsoon (habagat).

Mayor Jun Ynares said the rider was immediately brought to the Rizal Provincial Hospital System Antipolo Annex 2 for medical treatment.

The mayor said the incident occurred at Simeon Compound, in front of Clean Fuel in Grand Heights, Barangay San Roque.

Motorists were advised to avoid the area and use alternative routes while clearing operations are underway.

"Patuloy ang clearing operations para maalis ang mga nakaharang at maibalik sa normal ang daloy ng trapiko (Clearing operations are ongoing to remove the obstructions and restore normal traffic flow)," he said.

The mayor added that high rainfall volumes have also been recorded at various rainfall stations over the past week.

As of 12 p.m. on Sunday, the following rainfall totals were recorded over the past 24 hours:

*Antipolo (Capitol) station - 127.0 mm

*Bagong Nayon (COGEO) - 152.5 mm

*Bosoboso - 143.0 mm

He therefore reminded residents, especially those living in low-lying and flood-prone areas, to exercise caution, as the soil may have become saturated and unstable after days of rain, potentially causing soil erosion and landslides in mountainous and elevated areas.

The local government said it continues to monitor the situation together with the barangays.

Residents were advised to remain alert and immediately report any hazardous conditions in their areas.

title: UPLIFT beneficiaries allocate cash aid for food, medicine, home repairs
content_lead:
Beneficiaries of the UPLIFT cash aid program said the money would go to food, medicine, and home repairs.

Beneficiaries of the government's expanded Unified Package for Livelihoods, Industry, Food, and Transport (UPLIFT) program began claiming their cash aid on Monday, saying they will spend it on daily necessities and house repairs in preparation for the rainy season.

In Oscar Oida's "24 Oras" report, the cash aid distribution, spearheaded by the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), was simultaneously held across the country.

In Muntinlupa City, Luzviminda Gemina, 68, said that qualifying as a UPLIFT beneficiary was an "answered prayer," because she can finally fix their house, especially their roof that is full of holes.

"Nagulat na nga lang ako eh sa tagal ng panahon, ngayon lang ako nakatanggap. Nakatanggap man ako, sir, e bigas sa senior. Sakto po na makabili akong yero, kahit tatlo lang muna kasi ang kailangan na yero sa bahay ko, anim," Gemina said.

(I was surprised because this is the first time I've received something like this. Before, I only received the rice allowance for seniors. This is just in time for me to buy roofing sheets -- even just three for now, because my house actually needs six.)

Around 43 beneficiaries from Muntinlupa City received their P2,000 cash assistance on Monday. They were the only ones who showed up out of the 124 individuals who qualified in the program based on the Philippine Statistics Authority's 2024 community-based monitoring system.

According to local authorities, some of the qualified individuals can no longer be located.

"'Yung iba naman po nakakulong, 'yung iba nasa probinsya na po. Talagang mostly wala na po sila dito sa Muntinlupa," said Maritess Dumasena of the Social Service Department of Muntinlupa City.

title: Siblings cooking lunch killed in Rizal rockslide
content_lead:
Two siblings, aged 22 and 20, were killed after a boulder struck them while they were cooking lunch at the store where they worked during a rockslide in Sitio Wawa, Barangay San Rafael, Rodriguez, Rizal, on Wednesday, Aug. 5.

On Thursday, Aug. 6, Barangay Captain Judith Cruz told the Manila Bulletin that the siblings were with the 22-year-old female victim's husband before the incident. He had briefly left to fish near the store when the rockslide occurred around 12 p.m.

"Nangyari po yung incident doon sa tindahan po yun na kanilang pinag t-trabahuan. Nung 12, nagluluto yung magkapatid para sa tanghalian nila (The incident happened at the store where they worked. At around noon, the siblings were cooking their lunch when the incident occurred)," she said.

Cruz said the impact of the falling boulder was so strong that it hurled the female victim's body into the river, while her brother allegedly sustained fatal injuries.

She added that the boulder may have fallen from higher up, as there were reportedly no sounds of falling rocks before the incident. Only a single boulder was reported to have fallen.

"Walang narinig na parang nag-slide na bato, parang biglang deretso bagsak. So big sabihin (baka) ang taas ng pinanggalingan (There were no sounds of rocks sliding. It was as if the boulder suddenly fell straight down, so it may have come from much higher up)," she said.

Only the store where the victims were working at the time of the incident was affected by the falling boulder.

Cruz said the victims had also survived a rockslide last year, during which a boulder struck their home, although all members of the family escaped unharmed. She added that they had been advised to relocate from the area, but still went to Sitio Wawa for work.

She said she was saddened by the incident, noting that she had personally met and spoken with the female victim only recently, who was among those who received school supplies and rice from the barangay.

title: 64-year-old rescued after being swept away while crossing Rizal spillway
content_lead:
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.

A 64-year old senior citizen was swept away by strong currents while he was trying to cross a spillway in Rodriguez, Rizal.

In a "24 Oras" report by Jaime Santos, the elderly man was seen on the CCTV footage trying to cross the spillway. While another man was seen crossing safely, the senior citizen fell behind, struggling to get to the other side until he finally lost balance and fell into the water.

A few moments later, officials from Barangay San Rafael and the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (MDRRMO) responded to save the senior citizen.

Rescuers were tied to a rope as they rescued the old man.

"Nahihirapan lang po dahil kahit sabihin mong may part na mababaw, doon po sa malalim, nandoon po talaga ang malakas na current o agos ng tubig. Doon po kami nagtulung-tulong at tumawag na rin po sa MDRRMO para sa karagdagang salbabida at mga lubid," San Rafael Barangay chairperson Judith Cruz said.

(It was hard because even if you say that there is a part that is shallow, in the parts that are deeper, that is where the strong currents are. That is where we helped each other and called the MDRRMO for additional life vests and ropes.)

Cruz urged citizens to refrain from going to prohibited areas for their own safety.

Barangay rescuer Rolando Domingo said that it was hard to cross the spillway, but they were able to use their equipment to rescue the senior citizen within a few minutes.

The barangay said that the victim lost consciousness, but was given first aid before being brought to the hospital.

Many parts of the country have experienced continuous rains due to the combined effects of Tropical Storm Maymay and the Southwest Monsoon. Several areas have reported experiencing widespread floods and landslides. -- Jean Mangaluz/LDF, GMA News

title: Red Cross rescues 6 amid flooding in Rizal's low-lying areas
content_lead:
The rescued individuals were brought to the evacuation center by a rescue boat.

Some low-lying areas in Rizal Province were not spared as the heavy rains brought by the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat caused flooding.

According to Emil Sumangil's report in "24 Oras" on Monday, personnel from the Philippine Red Cross waded through waist-deep floodwaters, along with the strong winds and rain, to rescue six people in a household in Rodriguez, Rizal early morning.

The rescued individuals were brought to the evacuation center by a rescue boat.

In Barangay Burgos, also in Rodriguez, the floodwater was chest-deep after a nearby river overflowed.

"Last night, around 11 p.m., the water was already going down. This morning, around 5 or 6, it started rising again because the rain poured heavily again early this morning," said Barangay Kagawad JR Simbulan.

The barangay cleared the tree trunks and waste to help the floodwater to recede.

In San Mateo, residents were stranded after several roads became impassable due to flooding. The floodwater at Barangay Malanday was knee-deep at noon.

Although the weather slightly improved, the flood was still an inconvenience for many. For instance, the flood caused traffic along Felix Avenue.

But things were worse near Marcos Highway in Antipolo City as a subdivision became impassable for vehicles. A resident had to use a jetski to traverse within their community.

Not everyone are fortunate to have such a water vehicle. Many residents had no choice but to wade through the floodwaters to do their errands. They argued that paying for a boat o pedicab ride would be unreasonable.

title: Philippines: The Upwelling Wind - ICSF
content_lead:
Fishers are bringing the NPOA-SSF to life through local leadership, collective ownership and community action

This article is by Ronald B. Rodriguez (rrodriguez.icsf@gmail.com), Asia Region Programme Officer, ICSF, The Philippines

Over a decade removed from the adoption of the Voluntary Guidelines for Securing Sustainable Small-Scale Fisheries in the Context of Food Security and Poverty Eradication (SSF Guidelines, 2014), the Philippine small-scale fisheries (SSF) subsector stands at a critical juncture. The creation of the SSF Guidelines involved about 4,000 stakeholders from civil society groups in 120 countries in the UN FAO-led process to ensure that the voices, concerns and rights of actual fishers and fishworkers were embedded in the final document. Following the endorsement of the SSF Guidelines, The Philippines became in 2024 the first country in Asia to develop a National Plan of Action for Small-Scale Fisheries (NPOA-SSF). The NPOA-SSF, rooted in the SSF Guidelines, has evolved into a national instrument designed to address the specific vulnerabilities and aspirations of the country's small-scale fisheries.

In November 2025, a capacity-building workshop organized by Tambuyog Development Center, Inc. (Tambuyog), with the support of ICSF, signalled a momentous shift in sectoral governance strategy: rather than waiting for top-down directives, fisherfolk networks and local stakeholders resolved to take ownership of the NPOA-SSF to ensure it becomes a living document that genuinely serves fisherfolk communities.

Alternative pathways

Translating strategic ownership of a process into practice necessitates navigating the complex governance and socio-economic realities of the Philippine SSF subsector. The implementation of the NPOA-SSF occurs within a complex governance landscape. The GMA Kapuso Foundation has collected a total of 1,462 blood bags after a donation drive on August 8 in celebration of Mel Tiangco's birthday.

The "24 Oras" anchor is the GMA Kapuso Foundation Special Adviser and has been championing blood donation initiatives since 1996.

Among those who participated in the Sagip Dugtong Buhay project was Precious, an admin accounting officer for an advertising company.

"I promised myself before that I will continue donating as long as I can," she said.

The blood donation drive was conducted in partnership with the Philippine Red Cross.

"It will primarily go to our kiddie cancer champions," said Rikki Escudero-Catibog, EVP and COO of the GMA Kapuso Foundation. "The donated blood underwent a clean and thorough process by the Red Cross."

Philippine Red Cross Secretary General Gwendolyn Pang said this has been one of the biggest blood donation drives.

"We ensure that the blood will make it to different hospitals," she said.

Tiangco, who was not present as she was with her family, thanked the blood donors.

"I pray every year that your blood donations will give you good health and a life filled with blessings," she said.

The blood donors were given food, freebies, and a free bone scan.

title: 12,000 individuals affected by Habagat receive aid from GMA Kapuso Foundation
content_lead:
Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google.

Around 12,000 individuals affected by the southwest monsoon, or Habagat, have received assistance from the GMA Kapuso Foundation.

According to Mel Tiangco's report in "24 Oras" on Wednesday, among the beneficiaries is Thelma Serrano, a resident of Montalban, Rizal. She was forced to evacuate with her grandchildren after floodwaters quickly rose in their community due to the heavy rains.

Six years after Typhoon Ulyses struck Montalban, Thelma found herself reliving the trauma as the recent rains brought back memories of the devastating floods.

With no available transportation, Thelma immediately carried her grandchild to safety and evacuated with her six grandchildren.

"I didn't know where my grandchildren could get a ride because the water suddenly rose. I had to make sacrifices to make sure my grandchildren would be safe," she said.

They remain at an evacuation center as they wait for the floodwaters to subside.

Whenever the weather improves, Thelma and her husband return to their home to clean up. Their house was left covered in mud following the flooding.

Thelma hopes that her community will no longer experience severe flooding and called for improvements to the area's drainage system.

"Hopefully, the flooding in our area can be prevented. I hope the drainage systems can be fixed because some of them are still clogged."

Through its Operation Bayanihan program, the GMA Kapuso Foundation distributed food packs, biscuits, drinking water, and bread to evacuees in Montalban and San Mateo, Rizal.

title: Budget release rate hits 88% at end-June
content_lead:
THE Department of Budget and Management (DBM) said it released 87.9% of the budget for 2026 as of the end of June.

According to the DBM Status of Allotment Release report, the releases amounted to P5.97 trillion out of the original budget total of P6.79 trillion, leaving P819.49 billion undistributed.

The release rate at the end of last month was running behind the year-earlier pace of 90%.

Releases to government agencies and departments amounted to P3.34 trillion by the end of June, equivalent to 90.9% of their allocations, compared to 94% in the same period last year.

Special-purpose funds released by the end of the month stood at P477 billion, representing 66.3% of the total allotment.

Meanwhile, automatic appropriation releases were at 89.8%, or P2.15 trillion.

These include the National Tax Allotment of P1.19 trillion, the P712.5 billion in interest payments, the P93.98 billion for the Block Grant, the P82.92 billion for retirement and life insurance premiums, and the P36.47 billion for a special account in the general fund, which includes the P6 billion allotment for the Rice Competitiveness Enhancement program.

title: Bulog Usul MBG Pakai Beras Premium Kaya Vitamin, Ini Alasannya
content_lead:
Perum Bulog mengusulkan penggunaan beras premium yang diperkaya vitamin dan mineral sebagai bahan baku program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG).

Usulan tersebut akan dibahas lebih lanjut dalam rapat koordinasi terbatas (rakortas) di Kementerian Koordinator Bidang Pangan sebagai alternatif pasokan beras bagi dapur MBG menyusul larangan penggunaan beras subsidi Stabilisasi Pasokan dan Harga Pangan (SPHP) dalam program tersebut.

Direktur Utama Bulog Ahmad Rizal Ramdhani mengatakan usulan itu merupakan salah satu bentuk dukungan Bulog terhadap pelaksanaan MBG yang kini berada di bawah koordinasi Kepala Badan Gizi Nasional (BGN) Sudaryono.

"Ini dari Kementan agar Bulog mendukung MBG. Pak Sudaryono kan sekarang jadi kepala MBG kan. Jadi Bulog salah satu programnya ke depan akan membuat ini (beras premium khusus MBG)," kata Rizal di Kementerian Pertanian Jakarta Selatan, Selasa (28/7).

Rizal menjelaskan beras yang diusulkan bukan merupakan beras SPHP, melainkan beras premium khusus yang diperkaya berbagai vitamin dan mineral untuk membantu memenuhi kebutuhan gizi penerima manfaat MBG.

"Ini (beras) premium khusus. Kan kalau MBG kan tidak boleh beras subsidi. Jadi kami merencanakan konsepnya ini untuk mendukung program MBG sehingga ini mendukung anak-anak sekolah, anak-anak dan ibu hamil karena di beras tersebut kita tambahkan fortifikasi vitamin-vitaminnya," ujarnya.

[Gambas:Youtube]

Berdasarkan contoh kemasan yang ditunjukkan Rizal, produk tersebut diberi nama Beras Bergizi Premium untuk MBG. Beras itu diklaim diperkaya zat besi, asam folat, vitamin B1, B3, B6, B12, dan zinc.

Kemasan juga mencantumkan sasaran penerima manfaat, yakni balita, anak sekolah tingkat SD dan SMP, ibu hamil, serta kelompok penerima MBG lainnya. Produk dikemas dalam ukuran 5 kilogram dan mengusung konsep fortifikasi vitamin dan mineral untuk melengkapi kandungan gizi makanan.

Menurut Rizal, tambahan zat gizi tersebut diharapkan dapat melengkapi nutrisi dari lauk-pauk yang disajikan dalam menu MB

title: Lobi ke Kementan, Dharmasraya Dapat Bantuan Alsintan Senilai Rp20 Miliar - Harian Singgalang
content_lead:
JAKARTA - Upaya Pemerintah Kabupaten Dharmasraya melobi pemerintah pusat kembali membuahkan hasil. Dalam audiensi dengan pejabat Kementerian Pertanian di Jakarta, Senin (27/7/2026).

Bupati Dharmasraya Annisa Suci Ramadhani yang bertangan dingin kembali berhasil mengamankan tambahan bantuan alat dan mesin pertanian (alsintan) untuk mendukung produksi pangan di daerahnya.

Annisa bertemu Direktur Jenderal Prasarana dan Sarana Pertanian (PSP) Andi Nur Alam Syah serta Direktur Pascapanen Rizal Ismail. Pertemuan itu turut dihadiri Kepala Dinas Pertanian Dharmasraya Lasmiyati.

Bantuan yang dijanjikan pemerintah pusat mencakup dua unit UV Dryer berkapasitas 10 ton, satu Vertical Dryer, satu Combine Harvester, serta dua Power Thresher untuk mendukung penanganan pascapanen.

Untuk mengantisipasi kekeringan, Kementerian Pertanian juga mengalokasikan 20 unit pompa air enam inci dan 50 unit pompa air tiga inci. Sementara pada tahap prapanen, Dharmasraya memperoleh 10 unit traktor roda dua, lima unit traktor roda empat, serta satu unit drone pemetaan kawasan pertanian. Tambahan bantuan tersebut melengkapi berbagai program yang telah diperoleh sepanjang 2026. Nilai keseluruhan dukungan sektor pertanian dari pemerintah pusat tahun ini diperkirakan mencapai sekitar Rp20 miliar.

Selain alsintan, pemerintah daerah menyebut pembangunan Gudang Bulog di Dharmasraya akan segera direalisasikan. Fasilitas itu diharapkan meningkatkan kapasitas penyerapan gabah petani, menjaga stabilitas harga, sekaligus memperkuat rantai distribusi pangan di daerah.

Bagi Pemkab Dharmasraya, rangkaian pertemuan dengan kementerian merupakan bagian dari strategi untuk menarik lebih banyak program dan anggaran pusat.

Tantangan berikutnya adalah memastikan seluruh bantuan tersebut tepat sasaran, dimanfaatkan secara optimal, dan benar-benar berdampak pada peningkatan produktivitas serta kesejahteraan petani, bukan sekadar menambah daftar bantuan yang diterima daerah. (sp) Editor :

title: Bulog Klaim Stok Beras Aman Meski 35 Ribu Ha Sawah Terdampak El Nino
content_lead:
Direktur Utama Perum Bulog Ahmad Rizal Ramdhani memastikan sekitar 35 ribu hektare (ha) sawah yang terdampak El Nino tidak akan mengganggu ketersediaan beras nasional.

Menurutnya, cadangan beras pemerintah (CBP) yang saat ini tersimpan di gudang Bulog, ditambah potensi panen yang masih berada di lahan, dinilai cukup untuk memenuhi kebutuhan masyarakat hingga panen raya tahun depan.

"Dengan stok yang per hari ini sudah 5,25 juta ton ditambah dengan standing crop sekitar 10 juta ton ditambah dengan horeka juga 10 juta ton maka (total) 25,257 juta ton. Sedangkan kebutuhan makan orang Indonesia itu setahun adalah 22,5 juta ton. Jadi masih lebih. Estimasi kami nanti panen di bulan Maret 2027 kita masih ada stoknya," kata Rizal di kawasan Kalibata, Jakarta Selatan, Jumat (31/7).

Pernyataan itu merespons paparan Menteri Pertanian Andi Amran Sulaiman yang sebelumnya mengungkap sekitar 35 ribu hektare lahan pertanian mulai terdampak kekeringan akibat El Nino.

Meski demikian, pemerintah menilai luas lahan yang terdampak masih relatif kecil dan dapat diantisipasi melalui pompanisasi, perbaikan irigasi, serta dukungan cadangan pangan nasional.

Rizal mengatakan CBP yang saat ini mencapai 5,257 juta ton menjadi salah satu penyangga utama untuk menjaga pasokan apabila produksi sempat terganggu akibat cuaca.

Selain itu, pemerintah juga masih memiliki potensi produksi dari tanaman padi yang sedang tumbuh (standing crop) sekitar 10 juta ton, ditambah stok beras yang berada di sektor hotel, restoran, dan katering (horeka) sekitar 10 juta ton.

Dengan total ketersediaan tersebut, Bulog memperkirakan kebutuhan konsumsi beras nasional yang mencapai sekitar 22,5 juta ton per tahun masih dapat dipenuhi hingga memasuki musim panen berikutnya.

Di sisi lain, Rizal mengatakan Bulog terus mengejar target penyerapan beras sesuai Instruksi Presiden (Inpres) Nomor 4 Tahun 2026. Hingga 31 Juli, realisasi penyerapan beras telah mencapai 3,507 juta ton dari target 4 juta ton pada tahun ini.

JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com - Perum Bulog memastikan stok beras aman meski ada fenomena El Nino atau memanasnya suhu permukaan air laut.

Direktur Utama Perum Bulog Ahmad Rizal Ramdani, mengatakan hasil serapan sebesar 87,4 persen atau setara dengan 3,5 juta ton sudah dilaporkan ke Presiden Prabowo Subianto, Menteri Pertanian Andi Amran Sulaiman, dan Menteri Perekonomian Airlangga Hartarto.

"Dengan 3,5 juta ton itu, stok Bulog sekarang hampir mencapai 5,4 juta ton. Ditambah stok di Horeka dan lain sebagainya sekitar 10 juta ton, serta standing crop 10 juta ton, totalnya kurang lebih menjadi 25 sampai 26 juta ton," ucap Rizal ketika ditemui di Kantor Pusat Bulog, Senin (3/8/2026) malam.

title: DoST pushes urban farming technologies to strengthen Metro Manila food security
content_lead:
The Department of Science and Technology (DoST) on Thursday said it is offering several urban farming technologies that can be adopted in Metro Manila to help strengthen the region's food security.

DoST Secretary Renato U. Solidum Jr. said smart agriculture is not limited to large agricultural lands but can also be implemented in urban areas through greenhouse farming for high-value crops, vertical farming, and aquaculture, even with limited space and materials.

He said these smart farming methods can be adopted by communities as well as individual households.

"They can grow a wide variety of vegetables and even crayfish using drums. These technologies can be introduced even in your own home," Mr. Solidum said during a press conference of the National Capital Region's (NCR) Regional Science, Technology, and Innovation Week.

Mr. Solidum said the adoption of technology-driven solutions to boost food production and improve supply chains has become increasingly important as Metro Manila continues to face rising food prices, making food affordability and accessibility a challenge.

He said food prices in Metro Manila have increased by around 40% to 50% over the past decade.

Among the crops suitable for Metro Manila are oyster mushrooms, which do not require large amounts of space to cultivate, according to Romelen T. Tresvalles, regional director of DoST-NCR.

To make mushroom farming more viable in urban areas, DoST, in partnership with the Rizal Technological University (RTU), developed the Solar-Powered Automated Modular Mushroom Growing House. The technology is designed for easy community adoption as it is inexpensive, easy to assemble, requires minimal maintenance, and features an automated system for mushroom cultivation.

A community in Pasig City is among the beneficiaries of the technology.
